Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed head-on motor vehicle collision with complaints of neck and low back pain, stiffness,
and muscle guarding. Examination findings were consistent with cervical and lumbar strain, and the reported mechanism of
injury is well matched to the nature and force of the impact. Imaging studies clearly confirm the soft tissue injury and rule out
fracture or instability. The patient has no known prior injury to the cervical or lumbar regions. Care was delivered over fifteen
visits and included manual therapy, therapeutic exercise, and home stretching instruction, following a typical course of recovery.
Pain and range of motion improved steadily, and visit frequency was reduced as fucntion returned. Billing records reflect single
charges for each service rendered, with no duplicated or repeated billing. The patient was discharged to a self-directed home
execrise program with instructions to return if symptoms recur or worsen.
